route: Main.riemannHypothesis := rhOfAll := Formalism.VW.rh_of_every allChi (Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean*): RH from Dirichlet nonvanishing on Re s > 1/2 for every character (modulus 1 gives ζ) plus the functional equation of ζ for zeros to the left (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean). allChi := UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter. The zero-free step is zeroFree_of_rpow_window* (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/DedekindLFunctions/LandauTheorems/ZeroFreeOfRpowWindow.lean: a one-sided bound for a smoothed character-sum family on windows [Y, Y^(1+δ)] for arbitrarily large Y gives zero-freeness on Re s > θ), fed by window bounds whose exponent 1/2 + O(ε) is pushed below Re s. The arithmetic input is a statement named Row (Galois representations for regular algebraic polarized cuspidal data over CM fields), supplied through geometry and theta-lift constructions, with theta, local-matching, covolume and Galois-cohomology (a Vandiver-type length bound, VVle/VWin) estimates.

Names of fields are not evidence of what is proved.

* The bundle UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenLiteratureStatements (a Prop structure, line 215) has three fields: caraianiLocalGlobalDual and galoisRepOfPolarizedPairLit, both of the SAME type UpperTheory.One.M.Row, and localLanglandsExists. It is built as ⟨h, recTExists, h⟩: two literature names, one proposition. Most '..._of_literature O' theorems take the bundle as an argument and do not use it (their proofs call the release's own *_holds theorems).

Whether the release's Row is the theorem of the literature it is named after is a reading question (its own definitions); for the soundness of the five public theorems it does not matter — the kernels check the closure.

The Rallis chain theorem stmt3c is conditional on six premises, one requiring nonzero periods at every link (FunctionModelRallisFromInputs.lean, lines 534-566); the public theorems have no hypotheses, so wherever it is used its premises are discharged inside the closure.
